meta.title: Start Working Pontremoli — Work from a place you can call home
meta.description: Smart working community in Lunigiana, Tuscany. Free coworking, high-speed fiber, nature and real community.

hero.title: Work from a place you can call home.
hero.subtitle: A distributed community of remote workers in the heart of wild Tuscany.

ch1.title: How it all began
ch1.p1: October 2020. Two locals look around and see a town emptying out. Houses closing, young people leaving, shops shutting down. But they also see something the rest of the world is desperately searching for: space, silence, beauty, a life on a human scale.
ch1.p2: The insight was simple and revolutionary: you didn't need to bring people to the work. You needed to bring the work to the people. And so Start Working was born — a project to attract remote workers from all over Italy and the world to a village in the Tuscan Apennines.
ch1.p3: More than four years have passed since then. Over 150 people have relocated here, from every Italian region and dozens of different countries. In 2023, Start Working became a registered social promotion association (APS), recognized and supported by the Municipality of Pontremoli. It's not a company. It's not a startup. It's a community that decided to rewrite the rules.
ch1.img_alt: Panoramic view of Pontremoli and Lunigiana

ch2.title: Not the Tuscany you imagine
ch2.p1: Forget the rows of cypress trees and velvet hills. Lunigiana is a wild territory wedged between three regions — Tuscany, Liguria, Emilia-Romagna — where the Via Francigena crosses chestnut forests, crystal-clear rivers, perched castles and medieval villages that seem frozen in time.
ch2.p2: Time flows differently here. Mornings smell of woodland, evenings carry the sound of bell towers. The Apennine mountains merge with the Apuan Alps, offering breathtaking panoramas. And yet you're not isolated: within an hour's drive you can reach eight provincial capitals.
ch2.p3: Pontremoli, the northernmost town in Tuscany, is the heart of it all. A village of medieval towers and bridges, crossed by the Magra river, with a historic center that tells a thousand years of history at every corner.

ch3.title: A community waiting for you
ch3.p1: Over 150 people, ages 25 to 60, have chosen Pontremoli as home. They're not tourists. They're professionals, creatives, families who decided to live differently. And the extraordinary thing is that this community is truly waiting for you.
ch3.q_paola: "I've been here three years and my life has been transformed. I wouldn't go back for anything in the world."
ch3.p2: The connections here aren't superficial. It's not networking: it's real sharing. People have lunch together, explore trails on Saturdays, organize dinners and conversation evenings. Every month there's Start Talking, a gathering where old and new residents meet and exchange stories.
ch3.q_pierpaolo: "The connections here are authentic. It's not the usual networking: it's real life."
ch3.p3: Michelle came from Canada and found a rhythm she didn't know she was looking for. Alberto has been working from his desk with mountain views for twelve years. Andrea swears that testaroli improve his code quality. Ermes says it's not smart working here, it's smile working. And Letizia? She doesn't even need a car.
ch3.q_ermes: "This isn't smart working. It's smile working."

ch4.title: Your office in a 15th-century palace
ch4.p1: Imagine working under frescoed ceilings, in a hall that has witnessed centuries of history. Start Working's coworking space is located in Pontremoli's municipal palace, a 15th-century building provided free of charge by the municipality.
ch4.p2: Eight dedicated workstations, eight shared ones, a phone booth for calls, high-speed fiber optic. Open Monday to Saturday during office hours. But the coworking is much more than a desk: it's where daily life is shared. A coffee break becomes a conversation, a lunch becomes a friendship.
ch4.p3: And it's all free. No subscription, no hidden costs. The municipality manages the space because they believe that bringing remote workers means bringing life to the village.
ch4.img_alt: Coworking space in a historic palace

ch5.title: Everything within walking distance
ch5.p1: One of the most common fears: "But does a mountain village have everything you need?" The answer is yes. One kilometer away there's a hospital with an emergency room, surgery, and helipad. There are schools at every level, shops, banks, a pharmacy, cinema and theater.
ch5.p2: Pontremoli is connected to the world: the A15 motorway is minutes away, the La Spezia-Parma railway passes through, and the airports of Pisa (90 km), Genoa (110 km) and Florence (150 km) are easily reachable. Getting around is simpler than you think.
ch5.p3: The community also helps you find housing — from listings to introductions with landlords. And if you have children, know that there's support for nurseries and babysitting, because here parenthood is not a solitary challenge.
ch5.img_alt: Street in an Italian historic town center

ch6.title: Nature and adventure
ch6.p1: Close your laptop and in five minutes you're in the forest. Mountain biking through medieval villages, river trekking in the Stretti di Giaredo canyons, hiking along the Magra with emerald-green water flowing between rocks. The Apennine ridges offer views that stretch all the way to the Apuan Alps.
ch6.p2: For those who prefer gentler rhythms, there are gyms, yoga classes, and ancient pilgrimage routes — the Via del Volto Santo and the Via Francigena — that cross the territory. Every season has its character: autumn smells of chestnuts, winter covers the peaks with snow, spring explodes with green and summer invites you to the rivers.

ch7.title: Festivals, culture and testaroli
ch7.p1: In January the Disfida dei Falo lights up the sky: Pontremoli's neighborhoods ignite enormous bonfires in honor of the patron saint, and the winner is the one with the tallest flame. In August, Medievalis transforms the center into a journey through time — five days of celebration honoring the 1226 imperial charter, with parades, taverns and performances.
ch7.p2: And then there's the food. Tour Day is a traveling food festival that winds through restaurants and shops. In Mulazzo, Bancarel'vino celebrates local wines. Testaroli — Lunigiana's signature dish — are a local religion, served with pesto, olive oil or ragu.
ch7.p3: Cultural life doesn't stop at festivals. There's the municipal band, theater group, photography clubs, scouts, historical reenactments, Civil Protection, and the digital festival Futuro (da) Remoto. And every month, Start Talking brings the community together for an evening of exchange and discovery.

ch8.title: How to join us
ch8.p1: Joining Start Working is simple, and it costs nothing. The first step is writing to us: tell us who you are, what you do and what you're looking for. We respond to everyone, no algorithms and no filters.
ch8.p2: We'll organize an exploratory visit: a few days to discover Pontremoli, the coworking space, the community and the territory. You'll walk through the streets of the center, have lunch with the people who live here, see the space where you could work every day.
ch8.p3: If you decide to relocate, the community helps you: from finding a house to handling bureaucracy, from introductions with neighbors to your first grocery run. You'll never be alone in this transition.
ch8.p4: A few quick answers: Start Working is open to all ages and all professions. It's not an employment service — you need to already have your own job. The coworking is free and managed by the municipality. There are no mandatory membership fees. The only thing we ask is the desire to be part of something.

ch8.whatsapp_title: The heart of the project is the WhatsApp Community
ch8.whatsapp_intro: The WhatsApp community is the right place to start. It's open, informal, and the most direct way to get to know us and interact with those who already live here. Inside you'll find the Announcements board with all updates and events, the New Arrivals group where you can ask anything with no strings attached, and many other themed groups to explore. You don't have to introduce yourself right away: join, look around, and when you're ready take the first step. We're waiting for you.

ch8.form_message_placeholder: Tell us who you are, what you do and what you're looking for. If you'd like, include your name and phone number too.
